goals: Allow the exact curated vanilla foliage and growable-plant set to use the real horizontal surfaces of canonical Nibaru slabs while preserving each vanilla block's identity, state, lifecycle, growth, harvesting, replacement, and drops.

Delegate bonemeal on exact dry bottom native Nibaru slabs for canonical Grass Block, Moss Block, and Pale Moss Block through the corresponding Minecraft 26.2 substrate implementation without broadening material or geometry ownership.
scope: Maintain the exact C2 implementation from frozen legacy project lineage bf1af349a0e43a49f12279e8e49794a2e1423aac, including C1's canonical support resolution, half-height model/outline/targeting representation, survival behavior, narrow plant allowlist, tall-grass/large-fern growth, and nether-wart behavior.

Maintain C2's bounded canonical projection for Grass Block, Moss Block, and Pale Moss Block substrate bonemeal on exact dry bottom native slabs, including exact slab restoration/reconciliation and the existing half-height representation for generated petals, wildflowers, azaleas, moss carpet, and pale-moss carpet.
Retain exact C2 as the current runtime-untested candidate and exact C1 as the released, aggregate-focused-runtime-passed predecessor without representing either release as accepted.

exclusions: No new plant families, substrate families, bonemeal mechanics, generated outputs, geometry coverage, or block-family behavior beyond exact C2.
Nylium, top/double/waterlogged slabs, vertical slabs, CNM Steps, stairs, walls, arbitrary partial geometry, and unsupported materials remain outside substrate bonemeal.

Mushrooms, saplings and direct lowered-azalea tree growth, mangrove propagules, crops/farmland, sweet berry bushes, columns, arbitrary double plants, aquatic plants, lanterns, and other decorations remain deferred.

Nibaru retains canonical material/native-slab ownership and Block Geometry Extensions/CNM retain their own geometry and switching systems; this project adds no duplicate plant blocks, persisted offset state, registry-name parser, or competing material table.
Runtime deployment, Test Slot or Test Instance Manager changes, accepted-stack mutation, dedicated Workbench access, and protected gameplay-instance access during this migration.
